title: Throughput safety net and scaling regression triage
creator: Priya Shah
summary: Triage and remediation plan for a sudden drop in dedicated pool throughput caused by an autoscaler regression plus edge scheduling behavior. Deliver immediate safety nets and a prioritized set of long-term fixes to restore contractual throughput guarantees.
description: What happened: On 2026-03-09 22:14 UTC multiple dedicated pools reported sustained 30-60% throughput degradation for 45 minutes. User-facing errors were limited due to existing graceful degradation policies, but several enterprise customers reported reduced tps and elevated latency. The regression appears correlated with a recent autoscaler change that modified scale-down heuristics and a kernel scheduling tweak that changed pod placement across racks. This ticket covers incident triage, safety net rollouts, and post-incident actions.
mitigation_timeline:
2026-03-09 22:18 UTC - PagerDuty page; initial investigation started by on-call.
2026-03-09 22:25 UTC - Rolled temporary throttle to non-critical customers to preserve contractual capacity for reserved pools.
2026-03-09 22:40 UTC - Reverted autoscale scale-down threshold (hotfix ENG-64220) on a canary subset of pools; saw 18% recovery within 8 minutes.
2026-03-09 23:05 UTC - Deployed placement-affinity rollback to prevent cross-rack packing; throughput returned to baseline by 23:27 UTC.
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC - Post-incident standup; assigned action items and owners.
investigation_findings:
Signals: autoscaler events spiked with premature scale-downs when CPU fell briefly due to batching variance; placement optimizer started consolidating pods across fewer racks to reduce cross-node network egress but inadvertently reduced parallelism for KV cache hot shards.
Telemetry: token-per-second and open-calls metrics show transient bursts followed by lower sustained concurrency causing both lower throughput and increased token-latency variance.
Root-cause hypothesis: interaction between more aggressive packing (placement optimizer) + new scale-down logic produced lower effective instance-parallelism for specific customer request distributions, exposing a throughput regression under non-uniform request fanout.
immediate_actions_taken: 1) Rolled back scale-down threshold change (ENG-64220) on all affected dedicated pools. 2) Paused placement optimizer for dedicated fleet to restore rack-level distribution. 3) Applied emergency rate-limits for best-effort tiers to reserve headroom. 4) Increased autoscaler cooldown window to prevent oscillation during request bursts.
long_term_proposals:
- Add a throughput-protection mode in autoscaler that prioritizes maintaining reserved capacity for dedicated pools over aggressive bin-packing.
- Introduce a placement-constraints toggle segmented by customer SLA so Dedicated customers maintain cross-rack spread.
- Add synthetic workload tests that exercise KV-cache shard hotness and measure throughput under non-uniform fanout during PR CI.
- Improve telemetry: surface instance-parallelism, per-shard concurrency, and placement-entropy in the console.
- Run a controlled rollout strategy for placement and autoscale changes with automated canary throughput checks before broad rollout.
acceptance_criteria:
- Emergency safety-net (autoscale rollback + placement toggle) validated on 3 representative clusters with no regressions in P50/P95 latency or overall throughput.
- New autoscale throughput-protection feature merged and e2e-tested (unit+integration) with perf bench showing >=95% of contractual throughput under synthetic hot-shard workload.
- Console dashboard surfaces 'instance-parallelism' and 'placement-entropy' metrics for dedicated pools.
- Runbook updated with clear steps for capacity shortfall scenarios, including rapid rollback steps and criteria for emergency rate limiting.
